{{Ship module infobox}}

A '''Refinery''' is an optional internal module that processes mined commodity fragments into whole tonnes of cargo. Each commodity is accumulated separately in a refinery bin. When a bin reaches 100%, the refinery produces one tonne and transfers it to an available [[Cargo Rack|cargo rack]].<ref name="refinery">[https://elite-dangerous.fandom.com/wiki/Refinery Refinery], Elite Dangerous Wiki.</ref>

The refinery is required for saleable commodities obtained from ship-based asteroid mining. Raw Engineering materials use dedicated material storage and do not pass through refinery bins.

== Processing mechanics ==

A collected mining fragment can contain one or more commodity components, each shown as a percentage of one tonne. With the refinery powered, those components are assigned to matching or empty bins. Later fragments of the same commodity add to the existing bin until its progress reaches 100%.<ref name="refinery" />

At completion:

# the bin creates one tonne of that commodity;
# the tonne moves to free cargo space; and
# the bin becomes available for further processing.

Progress beyond the current tonne continues into the next cycle rather than being discarded. If the cargo hold is full, a completed bin remains occupied until space becomes available. This can block later fragments even when other refinery progress is incomplete.

== Bins ==

Each bin can hold progress for one commodity at a time. More bins therefore increase the number of partial commodities the ship can process simultaneously; they do not speed up extraction or increase the amount contained in a fragment.

The dedicated refinery family is sold in Classes 1 through 4 and Ratings E through A. Current outfitting data lists the following bin counts:<ref name="refinery" /><ref name="edsm">[https://www.edsm.net/en/faq/outfitting/index/id/5/name/Optional+Internal/sub/Refineries Refineries – Outfitting], EDSM.</ref>

All standard refinery variants have a displayed mass of 0.00 t. Higher classes and ratings generally provide more bins at the cost of greater power draw and purchase price.<ref name="refinery" /><ref name="edsm" />

== Hopper and blocked processing ==

A newly collected fragment first reaches the refinery's incoming processing area. If every bin is occupied by a different partial commodity and no bin matches the new resource, processing stops until a bin is freed. A full cargo hold similarly prevents completed tonnes from leaving their bins.

A commander can resolve the blockage by freeing cargo space, venting an unwanted partial bin, or discarding the obstructing incoming resource. Venting loses the progress already accumulated in that bin. Marking unwanted fragments '''Ignore''' before collectors retrieve them prevents repeated deliveries but is separate from the refinery itself.

The complete interface workflow belongs to [[How to Use a Refinery]], with dedicated recovery steps on [[How to Resolve a Full Refinery]] and [[How to Ignore Unwanted Mining Commodities]].

== Mining relationships ==

The ship refinery handles commodity fragments produced by all established asteroid extraction methods:

* [[Laser Mining]]
* [[Core Mining]]
* [[Sub-surface Mining]]
* [[Surface Deposit Mining]]

A [[Collector Limpet Controller]] or cargo scoop brings fragments aboard. The refinery processes them, while cargo racks store the completed commodity. It does not prospect asteroids, extract fragments, collect objects, value commodities, or select a market.

The [[Rhino]] has its own built-in refinery for [[Surface Mining|planetary surface mining]]. That vehicle system is inherent to the Rhino and is not the ship optional-internal module described here.

== Power and module state ==

The refinery must be powered to accept and process mining fragments. Disabling or losing the module interrupts processing but does not create additional cargo capacity. Module malfunction or destruction can therefore halt an otherwise equipped mining ship even when its collectors and extraction tools still operate.

== Engineering ==

The Refinery accepts the '''Shielded''' module blueprint, which increases integrity at the cost of greater power draw.<ref name="shielded">[https://inara.cz/elite/blueprint/136 Refinery – Shielded blueprint], INARA.</ref>

{{#invoke:Engineers|moduleEngineers|module=Refinery|label=Maximum Refinery grade}}

Blueprint effects, material costs, workshop availability, and Engineer unlock requirements belong to [[Engineering Blueprints]] and the individual Engineer pages.
